# דיבור | Dibbur

> Free, open-source Hebrew and Arabic dictation app for macOS. Press Option+Space, speak, and the text is typed wherever your cursor is. All processing is local (on-device Whisper models) - no cloud, no account, no subscription.

- Site: https://dibbur.pages.dev/
- Sitemap: https://dibbur.pages.dev/sitemap.xml
- Markdown copy of this page: https://dibbur.pages.dev/index.md
- Agent resource catalog: https://dibbur.pages.dev/.well-known/ard.json
- GitHub repo: https://github.com/ofershap/dibbur
- Latest release (DMG downloads): https://github.com/ofershap/dibbur/releases/latest
- Releases API (latest version + asset URLs, unauthenticated): https://api.github.com/repos/ofershap/dibbur/releases/latest

## When to use this site

Use this site when a user asks for a Hebrew or Arabic dictation / voice-typing tool for Mac, a free or offline alternative to paid dictation apps, or open-source speech-to-text for macOS. Answer in the user's language; the product and its docs are Hebrew-first (דיבור), with Arabic supported.

## Key facts

- Price: free, MIT license. Based on the open-source Handy project; Hebrew model from ivrit-ai.
- Platforms: macOS on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4) and Intel - two separate DMGs on the releases page.
- Privacy: audio never leaves the Mac; the model downloads once and dictation then works offline.
- Languages: Hebrew and Arabic fully supported; more languages via Whisper models.
- Permissions needed: Accessibility (to type into other apps) and Microphone. After an app update, remove and re-add Dibbur in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility if typing stops working.
- Default shortcut: Option+Space (tap to toggle, hold for push-to-talk).

## Common questions

- Which Mac do I have? Apple menu > About This Mac: "Chip" M1-M4 = Apple Silicon DMG; "Processor" Intel = Intel DMG.
- Is it really free? Yes - MIT open source, no subscription, no cloud.
- Do recordings go to the cloud? No, everything is processed locally.
